w:r.w:t: [Gives the overall description about the product with some introduction and the context diagram. The context diagram presents the boundary and connections between the system you’re developing and everything else in the universe. This identifies external entities (or terminators – software, hardware, human components, and other systems) outside the system that interface to it in some way, as well as data, control, and material flows between the terminators and the system.]

<<Sample: The Cafeteria Ordering System is a new software system that replaces the current manual and telephone processes for ordering and picking up meals in the Process Impact cafeteria. The context diagram below illustrates the external entities and system interfaces for release 1.0. The system is expected to evolve over several releases, ultimately connecting to the Internet ordering services for several local restaurants and to credit and debit card authorization services.

This part gives the description of system actors, you can follow the table form as below]

End-user (non-technical) accessing the self-service booking portal to create APPOINTMENT records via web UI. Primary interactions: view available time slots, select physician, submit appointment request. Technical dependencies: responsive web interface, real-time availability validation, email/SMS confirmation (if implemented). Data owned: PATIENT demographics, parent_contact_phone.

Administrative user managing front-desk operations via Receptionist workflow UI. Core responsibilities: CRUD operations on PATIENT records, APPOINTMENT scheduling/status updates (Pending→Confirmed→Completed/Cancelled), BILLING payment processing (cash payments, mark as Paid/Unpaid), and exception handling for walk-ins/phone bookings. Technical requirements: role-based access control, audit logging, data validation rules.

Clinical end-user interacting with the EMR (Clinician view) to document patient care. Key workflows: retrieve PATIENT medical history (performance requirement: <2s load time), create VISIT records (symptoms, diagnosis, clinical_notes), generate PRESCRIPTION orders, and review BILLING status. Technical needs: optimized read queries, data persistence, and secure PHI access controls.

Technical operator with superuser privileges managing application lifecycle. Responsibilities include: system configuration (clinic settings, physician roster via admin UI), user account provisioning (if authentication enabled), database backup/restore operations, and application maintenance. Handles feature flag management, system health monitoring, and coordinates with DevOps for deployments. Technical access: full CRUD across all 5 entities, admin-only REST API endpoints, and access to audit logs.
[A use case (UC) describes a sequence of interactions between a system and an external actor that results in the actor being able to achieve some outcome of value. The names of use cases are always
written in the form of a verb followed by an object. Select strong, descriptive names to make it evident from the name that the use case will deliver something valuable for some user.
Following are some questions you might ask to help user representatives identify use cases
What will the actor use the system for?
Will the actor create, store, change, remove, or read data in the system?
Will the actor need to inform the system about external events or changes?
Will the actor need to be informed about certain occurrences in the system?
This part describes the use cases you could define, you can follow the table form as below]

Primary Flow: 1) Parent accesses booking portal. 2) Selects available time slot from calendar UI. 3) Selects physician (optional). 4) Enters child's PATIENT info (name, DOB). 5) Submits request → System creates APPOINTMENT record with status=Pending, sends confirmation (email/SMS if implemented). Alternate Flow: Slot unavailable → show alternatives. Business Rule: Appointment must be 15min minimum, max 30 days in advance.

Primary Flow: 1) Receptionist opens patient registration form. 2) Enters PATIENT demographics (name, DOB, parent_contact_phone, basic_medical_history). 3) Validates required fields. 4) Saves → System creates new PATIENT record with unique ID. Alternate Flow: Duplicate patient detection by name/DOB → prompt to merge or create new. Business Rule: Parent phone number required for SMS reminders (if enabled).

Primary Flow: 1) Physician selects patient from schedule or searches by ID. 2) Reviews APPOINTMENT details. 3) Enters consultation data (symptoms, diagnosis, clinical_notes) into VISIT record. 4) Saves → System creates VISIT record linked to PATIENT and APPOINTMENT. Alternate Flow: Missing PATIENT data → prompt to register first; Invalid diagnosis format → validation error. Business Rule: Diagnosis must be selected from ICD-10 code list; Clinical notes mandatory for billing.

Primary Flow: 1) Receptionist or Parent views completed VISIT. 2) Reviews consultation fee. 3) Records payment (cash/card). 4) Updates BILLING.status → Paid. System generates receipt. Alternate Flow: Partial payment → mark as Unpaid with balance_due; Card declined → retry or record as cash. Business Rule: BILLING record created automatically on APPOINTMENT completion; total_amount = consultation_fee.

Primary Flow: 1) Physician during/after consultation enters PRESCRIPTION (medicine_name, dosage_instruction, duration_days). 2) System validates required fields. 3) Saves → PRESCRIPTION record linked to VISIT. Alternate Flow: Incomplete dosage → prompt to fill; Allergy conflict → alert physician. Business Rule: All prescriptions require active VISIT; medicine_name must match formulary database (if implemented).

Primary Flow: 1) Physician or Receptionist searches PATIENT by ID/name. 2) System returns patient profile with demographics. 3) User views chronological list of APPOINTMENTs, VISITs, PRESCRIPTIONs. 4) Optional: Filter by date range or visit type. Alternate Flow: No records found → show "no history" message; Multiple matches → display disambiguation list. Business Rule: Only authorized clinical staff can view full history; Parents can only view their own children's records.

Primary Flow: 1) Parent or Receptionist selects APPOINTMENT. 2) Confirms cancellation intent. 3) System updates status → Cancelled. 4) Optionally triggers notification to physician. Alternate Flow: APPOINTMENT already Completed → cannot cancel; Cancellation within 24h → require manager override. Business Rule: Cancelled slots released immediately for booking; Cancellation fee may apply if within 24h of appointment.

Primary Flow: 1) Administrator accesses settings module. 2) Modifies system parameters (consultation fees, physician schedules, clinic information). 3) Saves changes → System updates configuration. Alternate Flow: Invalid data → validation error; Conflicting schedule → alert and prevent save. Business Rule: Only ADMIN role can access; All changes logged in audit trail.

[Provide common business rules that you must follow. The information can be provided in the table format as the sample below]
Delivery time windows are 15 minutes, beginning on each quarter hour.
Deliveries must be completed between 10:00 A.M. and 2:00 P.M. local time, inclusive.
All meals in a single order must be delivered to the same location.
All meals in a single order must be paid for by using the same payment method.
If an order is to be delivered, the patron must pay by payroll deduction.

Order price is calculated as the sum of each food item price times the quantity of that food item ordered, plus applicable sales tax, plus a delivery charge if a meal is delivered outside the free delivery zone.
Only cafeteria employees who are designated as Menu Managers by the Cafeteria Manager can create, modify, or delete cafeteria menus.
Network transmissions that involve financial information or personally identifiable information require 256-bit encryption.
Only regular employees can register for payroll deduction for any company purchase.
An employee can register for payroll deduction payment of cafeteria meals if no more than 40 percent of his gross pay is currently being deducted for other reasons.
